positions.name: AuthorityOverKestrelwoodRecord
positions.frame: Who holds the authority to decide what the record retains, what it must forget, and what actually happened?
positions.why: The relational read marks all three expressions authority-ranking: src-1 and src-2 command erasure ('Forget…', 'Remove all knowledge…') with decision-level conviction and pressure-register force, while src-3 closes the sequence with a flat, claim-level assertive ('The observatory never calibrated it') that supplies the justifying fact for the erasure rather than commanding it. The tension worth holding here is speech-act type: two performative directives claiming unilateral control over what the record must NOT contain, paired with one declarative claim asserting what did NOT occur — different illocutionary force (command vs. assertion), same authority move over the institutional record. Value dimension echoes this split: autonomy (self-directed erasure) on src-1/src-2 versus conservation (fixing the canonical account) on src-3 — two faces of the same authority claim.
